items.title: Compass vows to press on with FDA application despite new trial request
items.snippet: Citing the urgent unmet need for patients with advanced biliary tract cancer, Compass Therapeutics will continue to seek an approval path for its drug after the FDA recommended the biotech conduct a new clinical study.

items.title: Viking achieves 'maintenance trifecta' as GLP-1/GIP dual agonist exceeds expectations
items.snippet: Viking Therapeutics’ VK2735 met Truist’s “best-case scenario,” with robust weight loss that was largely maintained when patients transitioned to less frequent dosing. Viking’s stock popped more than 30% on Tuesday.

items.title: Vertex opens up larger kidney disease opportunity with mid-stage readout
items.snippet: While Vertex is laser-focused on an upcoming FDA decision for povetacicept in immunoglobulin A nephropathy, the APOL1 inhibitor inaxaplin has demonstrated potential “best-in-class” data in a different kidney disease.

items.title: Novo targets 10-fold jump in oral Wegovy manufacturing capacity by 2030
items.snippet: With sales of the oral GLP-1 medicine rising quickly, executives reassured investors that Novo has secured production capacity to support continued growth.

items.title: Lilly presents early data supporting GLP-1/GIP candidate's potential in depression, alcohol use disorder
items.snippet: With a trillion-dollar market cap and a wildly successful GLP-1 portfolio, Eli Lilly isn’t resting on its laurels. At the Psych Congress 2026, the company presented early-stage data that could support the potential of its next-gen GLP-1 and GIP receptor agonist to treat diseases far beyond obesity.

items.title: 2026 IPO blitz continues with 4 new biotech filings
items.snippet: With more than 25 companies debuting on the public markets, 2026 has recorded the highest number of biotech IPOs since 2021. Now, four companies—including Iambic Therapeutics and ADARx Pharmaceuticals—are looking to grow this total even further.

items.title: Novo’s workforce reduction climbs to 13,000 to fuel R&D work
items.snippet: Novo CEO Maziar Mike Doustdar disclosed an additional 4,000 staff departures, which a spokesperson told BioSpace are linked to attrition and other measures.

items.title: Roche’s Carmot asset normalizes blood sugar, cuts weight in Phase 2 diabetes trial
items.snippet: The mid-stage readout is one link in a chain of catalysts that analysts were watching for this year from Roche’s metabolic pipeline, which features assets from the $2.7 billion acquisition of Carmot Therapeutics as well as partner Zealand Pharma.

items.title: Boehringer Ingelheim bets up to $1B in AI-centered solid tumor collab with Envisagenics
items.snippet: Envisagenics’ platform makes use of AI to screen and detect cancer-specific RNA alterations, which Boehringer Ingelheim wants to target through various precision treatment modalities, including multi-specific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates and T cell engagers.

items.title: BMS says goodbye to 265 New Jersey staff as reorg rolls on
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: Deep Dive: How AI is now essential in biopharma
items.snippet: As Big Pharma adds AI technology to bolster drug development, a cadre of new, upstart biotechs are pushing drug discovery to new heights.

items.title: Western licensing deals for Chinese radioligand therapies to jump in 2027, Sleuth forecasts
items.snippet: Deals for Chinese radiopharmaceutical assets have been rare to date and there is a limited pool of potential Western buyers available, Sleuth said.

items.title: Novo’s plan to hit $23B in revenue by 2035 leaves investors wanting
items.snippet: Novo has “gone shopping” to fill pipeline gaps, with a focus on obesity and diabetes, plus an expansion in blood and endocrine disorders, liver diseases and cardiovascular conditions.

items.title: Telix buys ITM for $1.65B in ‘supercritical’ radiopharma M&A
items.snippet: Aside from its manufacturing and distribution footprint, ITM Isotope Technologies Munich will give Telix Pharmaceuticals the late-stage ITM-11, being developed for gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. The asset was rejected by the FDA last month for manufacturing concerns.

items.title: Novo buys three early-stage obesity assets from Kallyope as investor pressure mounts
items.snippet: Investors and analysts have been hounding Novo to beef up its pipeline and advance new molecules as a majority of the company's sales stem from its semaglutide franchise.

items.title: Citing Replimune approval, experts say localized cancer meds could redefine care
items.snippet: Delivering therapeutics directly to tumors, as in the case of Replimune’s recently approved Tudriqev and Amgen’s Imlygic, holds advantages, especially when cancer is caught early, but challenges remain before the method becomes a mainstay in treatment.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis on board with regulatory framework tailored to rare disease therapies
items.snippet: Newly permanent CBER and CDER directors Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis are widely expected to continue the FDA’s efforts toward an adaptive framework for rare disease therapies. If approved by the Senate, will commissioner nominee Heidi Overton stay the course?

items.title: Beyond Random Integration: Transposase cell line development shortening timeline & boosting titers
items.snippet: As molecule complexity rises, advanced cell line development platforms are giving biopharma companies new tools to overcome expression challenges, improve stability and reach the clinic faster.

items.title: China plans to transform biotech sector into $522B powerhouse by 2030
items.snippet: A new five-year biotech plan has been released by the Chinese government, revealing ambitious goals such as achieving five blockbuster medicines on the global markets in that time.

items.title: Electra lights up with $350M IPO for pivotal immune-disease drug development
items.snippet: Electra Therapeutics has exceeded its initial fundraising plans as it becomes the 26th biotech to debut publicly this year and outlines pivotal development plans for its monoclonal antibody ipsoprubart.

items.title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
items.snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

items.title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
items.snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.
